title: Prompt to answer
fullTitle: What Happens Between Your Prompt and the Answer?

scenes.narration: You ask: how many open support tickets are high priority? Back comes: five. Between that question and that number sit several parts. The model is only one.
captions: "How many open support tickets are high priority?" → 5
Between question and number sit several parts. The model is only one.

scenes.narration: First the application, not the model, assembles the request: a system message, your question, and one tool definition: count tickets by status and priority. Nothing else is offered.
captions: The application assembles: system message, question, one tool definition.
countTickets(status, priority). Nothing else is offered.

scenes.narration: The model replies, simulated here. It does not answer; it requests the tool with structured arguments: status open, priority high. We show the request, not private reasoning.
captions: The model does not answer. It requests the tool.
countTickets({status: "open", priority: "high"}) — the request, not private reasoning.

scenes.narration: The application checks it against the schema. Tool offered? Values allowed? Nothing extra? An unknown tool or unexpected key is refused before anything runs.
captions: Validate against the schema: tool offered? values allowed? nothing extra?
Unknown tool or unexpected key: refused before anything runs.

scenes.narration: Then the data scope. Whose tickets? That comes from the session, never from the model. A model-supplied account ID is rejected by the schema and ignored by the scope layer anyway.
captions: Data scope comes from the session, never from the model.
A model-supplied accountId is rejected, and ignored anyway.

scenes.narration: Now the tool runs: a narrow, read-only function. Two allowed filters, plus the organisation from the session. No SQL. The model never touches the data store.
captions: The tool runs: narrow, read-only. Two filters + the session's org.
No SQL. The model never touches the data store.

scenes.narration: A structured result returns: count, five. The application hands it back to the model, linked by one opaque request ID.
captions: Structured result: { count: 5 } returns to the application, then to the model.
One opaque request id links every step.

scenes.narration: The final message, again simulated, embeds that result: five. The fixture holds thirteen across all organisations; this user sees only their own five.
captions: Final answer embeds the computed count: 5.
13 open high-priority tickets exist across all orgs; this user sees only their own 5.

scenes.narration: Replay with a failing ticket store. One bounded retry, safe only because counting is read-only; state-changing tools need different care. Still failing? An honest answer: no count available. Nothing invented.
captions: Tool failure: one bounded retry (safe only because the tool is read-only).
Still failing: honest message, no count. Nothing invented.

scenes.narration: One application design, not every AI request. But the shape holds. The model requests the tool. The application controls execution.
captions: One application design, not every AI request.
The model requests the tool. The application controls execution.
